what:
THE ARBITRATION-FANOUT SOAK HAS WRITTEN NOTHING FOR 32 HOURS WHILE ITS MODE READS `apply`, AND NOTHING ALERTED. Found while verifying E17 before acting on it, not by a watcher -- which is itself the finding.
MEASURED 2026-09-24T09:55Z, three independent reads:
  (1) diag log_file arbitration_fanout_soak (#12820): newest row 2026-09-23T01:52:51Z. size_bytes 1,413,493 at /data/bot-data/runtime_logs/arbitration_fanout_soak.jsonl. The last 35 rows span 2026-09-22T16:51 -> 2026-09-23T01:52.
  (2) get-env ARBITRATION_FANOUT_MODE (#12822): process 'apply', declared 'apply'. ARMED.
  (3) get-env ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS (#12804): all 11 accounts present including breakout_1, process and declared agreeing.
WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A QUIET PERIOD, read from code rather than assumed: src/runtime/intent_multiplexer.py calls arbitration_fanout_soak.record() on EVERY arbitration where a winning intent is decided. record() returns early ONLY on mode == 'off'. It is NOT gated on >=2 candidates -- that is allocator_soak's contract, not this one. So 'nothing contested happened' does not explain 32 hours of nothing.
[!] AND THE REASON NOBODY NOTICED IS DESIGNED IN: the record() call site is wrapped in a bare except that swallows everything, with the comment 'observe-only soak must never break a tick'. That is the right call for tick safety and it makes a BROKEN SOAK INVISIBLE -- it fails exactly as silently as it succeeds. A soak whose failure mode is indistinguishable from its quiet mode is the collapsed-state defect this repo names as a bug class, sitting on an observability surface.
WHAT IT COSTS RIGHT NOW: E17's entire diagnosis rests on this log (apply_scope {breakout_1: 'not_allowlisted'}, starved_count 1) and CANNOT BE REPRODUCED, so that row is blocked on this one. More broadly the arbitration fanout is a LIVE ORDER-ELECTION path and its only observability surface has been dark for 32 hours.
[!] NOT ESTABLISHED, and do not let a lane assume any of it: whether the WRITE is failing, whether arbitration is still running at all, or whether a log rotation moved the file. Three different causes, three different fixes. Candidate to rule out first: ict-shadow-log-rotate.service. The diag read returned 1.4MB of OLD content at the canonical path, which argues against a fresh rotated file existing there -- but that is an inference, not a measurement.

── [RESOLUTION 2026-09-24, E50 lane session_019mw6kFz9EL3AuHL1AUT4ff] THE PREMISE WAS WRONG: THE SOAK WAS NEVER DARK.
MEASURED 2026-09-24 ~11:05Z by DIRECT read (scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh, served by https://ict-bot.duckdns.org, no relay, no truncation), log_file?name=arbitration_fanout_soak&lines=1000: 1000 rows, 2026-09-02T18:53:59Z -> 2026-09-24T11:00:15Z, size_bytes 1,418,802. Rows with logged_at_utc strictly inside (2026-09-23T01:52:51Z, 2026-09-24T09:48:01Z) = 65, all global_mode 'apply' and plan_state 'planned' (48 apply_state 'dispatchable', 17 'no_allowlisted_account'), across 13 symbols (BTCUSDT 17, AVAXUSDT 12, ETHUSDT 7, MGC 7, QQQ 5, ...). Positive control: allocator_soak (same multiplexer tick, same runtime_logs dir) also writing through the window, last row 2026-09-24T08:06:17Z.
CAUSE, established: #12820's path was `log_file?name=arbitration_fanout_soak&limit=40`. `limit` is not a parameter of /api/diag/log_file (it takes `lines`), so the endpoint returned its DEFAULT 100-row tail = 149,082 pretty bytes. scripts/ops/diag_relay_render.py then cut the bulk with json.dumps(bulk)[:remaining] -- a HEAD cut -- keeping the first 35 rows (oldest) and ending mid-row, and its marker said only that `lines` was 'cut'. The 35th row, 2026-09-23T01:52:51Z, was read as the newest. REPRODUCED: reconstructing that 100-row tail from the direct read (rows < 09:48:01Z, last 100) gives EXACTLY 149,082 pretty bytes -- the figure the #12820 marker printed -- and the old renderer's visible rows end at 01:52:51Z.
RULED OUT, therefore, and not needing separate evidence: a failing write, arbitration not running, and a rotation (ict-shadow-log-rotate) moving the file -- the file at the canonical path carries contiguous rows through the window.
FIX (Tier-1, scripts/**): the renderer now cuts lists at WHOLE elements and prints, per container, 'ONLY THE FIRST n of N element(s) are shown; the LAST N-n -- including the final one -- are NOT ... the last entry visible here is NOT the latest'. Self-test carries the #12820 shape plus a negative control on the old cut.
E17'S READING (d), reported not acted on: over the same 1000-row population, 109 rows grade breakout_1 (all 'starved'). apply_scope.breakout_1 = 'not_allowlisted' on 107, last 2026-09-22T08:24:49Z; = 'allowlisted' on 2, 2026-09-23T14:12:15Z and 15:02:00Z (ETHUSDT, winner trend_donchian_eth), and on BOTH the round (trend_donchian_eth_prop -> [breakout_1]) is in rounds_written AND rounds_applied (accepted by the dispatcher's validator). Whether an ORDER followed is NOT established -- per the soak docstring that needs a journal row.
The separate, still-true observation -- record() failures are swallowed at DEBUG so a broken soak WOULD look idle -- is filed as PI-20260924-L1AUT4FF-0001; it is not what happened here.
